findings.description: When a match is found and len(tokens) < width, len(tokens) - width is negative, so min() returns a negative start. The slice tokens[start:end] then uses negative indexing and returns the wrong words, usually an empty or truncated snippet. Also start > 0 is False, and end < len(tokens) can be True, so the truncation flags are wrong. Likewise, a hit near the start gives hit - width//2 < 0, so the window is anchored on a negative index instead of 0.
findings.suggestion: Clamp the start: start = max(0, min(hit - width // 2, len(tokens) - width)).
findings.title: Window start can be negative when the body is shorter than width
